problem: Long-instruction VLN (R4R, RxR) suffers from misalignment between action words in instructions and visual observations that lack explicit action cues, and between global instructions and the agent's local observation at each step.
motivation: Long instructions and extended trajectories make it hard to ground the correct part of the instruction at each step. Visual candidates carry no explicit action information while instructions are action-oriented, and the whole-trajectory instruction does not match a single local view.
key_idea: Encode candidate actions with relative heading and elevation angles into visual perception (ACEM), and dynamically reweight instruction words according to the current visual observation (DIWM).
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract implies that making actions explicit in visual features and focusing on instruction words relevant to the current view together improve alignment, giving SR gains of 8.5% on R4R and 4.0% on RxR.
method: Action-Perception Alignment Framework (APAF): overall framework addressing action misalignment and global-local misalignment in long-instruction VLN
Action-Contextual Encoding Module (ACEM): enriches visual perception of each candidate by encoding potential actions using relative heading and elevation angles
Dynamic Instruction Weighting Module (DIWM): adjusts the importance of instruction words conditioned on the current visual observation, emphasizing the most relevant words

setting.observation: panoramic RGB (presumed from discrete-view VLN; not stated in abstract)
setting.action_space: not specified in abstract (candidate viewpoints with heading/elevation)

results: The abstract claims state-of-the-art on long-instruction R4R and RxR, with SR improvements of 8.5% and 4.0% over existing methods. Absolute numbers and the strongest baseline are not given in the abstract.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so details, absolute metrics and ablations could not be verified
Evaluated on long-instruction benchmarks (R4R, RxR); generalization to other settings is not shown in the abstract
